message.content:
Search the /app repository (a Carbon-design-system-like monorepo) for the shared date & time formatting utilities. I'm looking for source files that implement formatters for: relative time, absolute time, absolute date, absolute date-and-time (combined), and date/time range formatting. They likely use Intl.RelativeTimeFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat, take an options object with `locale` and `style`, and are exposed through a public index/barrel.

Report back:
1. The exact file paths for each formatter's source.
2. The public export surface (index files / barrel) that consumers import from — full paths.
3. For each formatter: its default `style` value and how the style maps to Intl options.
4. Any related test files and any demo/example pages (look under examples/, docs/, stories, .mdx, storybook) that render these utilities.
5. The exact directory/module where I would add a new "duration" formatter following the same conventions.

Be thorough and give exact file paths and relevant code excerpts (the function signatures, default values, and export lines).

63	
64	### Date and time
65	
66	- Supported styles: `"full" | "long" | "medium" | "short" | "tooltip"`
67	  - `"tooltip"` is a shortand for `timeStyle: "long", dateStyle: "full"`
68	- Supported time styles: `"full" | "long" | "medium" | "short"`
69	- Supported date styles: `"full" | "long" | "medium" | "short"`
70	- Default time style: `"short"`
71	- Default date style: `"medium"`
72	
73	```js
74	import { dateTimeFormat } from '@carbon/utilities';
75	
76	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp);
77	// Apr 4, 2024 at 3:47 PM
78	
79	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp, { locale: 'de-DE' });
80	// 04.04.2024, 15:47
81	
82	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp, {
83	  timeStyle: 'medium',
84	  dateStyle: 'short',
85	});
86	// April 4, 2024 at 3:47:12 PM
87	
88	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp, { style: 'short' });
89	// 4/4/24, 3:47 PM
90	
91	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp, { style: 'tooltip' });
92	// Thursday, April 4, 2024 at 3:47:12 PM GMT+2
93	```
94	
95	### Range
96	
97	- Supported styles: `"full" | "long" | "medium" | "short"`
98	- Supported time styles: `"full" | "long" | "medium" | "short" | null`
99	- Supported date styles: `"full" | "long" | "medium" | "short" | null`
100	- Default time style: `"short"`
101	- Default date style: `"medium"`
102	
103	```js
104	import { dateTimeFormat } from '@carbon/utilities';
105	
106	dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatRange(startDate, endDate);
107	// Apr 4, 2024, 3:47 PM – Apr 25, 2024, 4:29 PM
108	
109	dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatRange(startDate, endDate, { locale: 'de-DE' });
110	// 04.04.2024, 15:47 – 25.04.2024, 16:29
111	
112	dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatRange(startDate, endDate, {
113	  timeStyle: 'medium',
114	  dateStyle: 'short',
115	});
116	// 4/4/24, 3:47:12 PM – 4/25/24, 4:29:38 PM
117	
118	dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatRange(startDate, endDate, { style: 'short' });
119	// 4/4/24, 3:47 PM – 4/25/24, 4:29 PM
120	```
121	
122	#### Date only
123	
124	The time can be omitted to only display the date range.
125	
126	```js
127	import { dateTimeFormat } from '@carbon/utilities';
128	
129	dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatRange(startDate, endDate, { timeStyle: null });
130	// Apr 28, 2016 – Jul 1, 2018
131	```
132	
133	#### Time only
134	
135	The date can only be omitted if the day is the same between start and end.
136	
137	```js
138	import { dateTimeFormat } from '@carbon/utilities';
139	
140	dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatRange(startDate, sameDayEndDate, {
141	  dateStyle: null,
142	});
143	// 3:47 – 4:29 PM
144	```
145	
146	#### Timezone
147	
148	For `absolute` functions, you can provide `timeZone` as an optional property.
149	This is useful when (for example) you want to display utc time instead of a
150	local timezone.
151	
152	```js
153	import { dateTimeFormat } from '@carbon/utilities';
154	
155	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp);
156	// Apr 4, 2024 at 3:47 PM
157	
158	dateTimeFormat.absolute.format(timestamp, { timeZone: 'UTC' });
159	// Apr 4, 2024 at 10:47 PM
160	```
161	
162	Timezone options are according to
163	[ECMAScript® 2026 Internationalization API Specification](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#datetimeformat-objects)

content.text:
All findings below. The utilities live in a single module: `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/`.

## 1. Formatter source files

All formatters live in two source files:

**`/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/relative.ts`** — relative time
```ts
export function format(
  date: Date | number,
  options?: Partial<{ locale: string; style: Intl.RelativeTimeFormatStyle }>
): string {
  const rtf = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(options?.locale, {
    style: options?.style ?? 'short',
  });
  ...
}
```

**`/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/absolute.ts`** — the other four:
- `formatTime` — absolute time (`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeStyle`)
- `formatDate` — absolute date (`dateStyle`)
- `format` — combined date-and-time (`timeStyle` + `dateStyle`, plus a `'tooltip'` shorthand)
- `formatRange` — date/time range (`dtf.formatRange(start, end)`)

## 2. Public export surface (barrels)

- `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/index.ts` — module barrel:
  ```ts
  import * as relative from './relative';
  import * as absolute from './absolute';
  export const dateTimeFormat = { relative, absolute };
  ```
- `/app/packages/utilities/src/index.ts` (line 11) — package root barrel: `export * from './dateTimeFormat';`
- `/app/packages/utilities/package.json` (`exports` field, lines 27–43) — published entry: `.` → `./es/index.js`, plus a wildcard `./*` subpath map.

Consumers import as: `import { dateTimeFormat } from '@carbon/utilities';` then `dateTimeFormat.relative.format(...)` / `dateTimeFormat.absolute.formatTime(...)` etc. (No other packages in the repo currently consume it — the earlier `@carbon/utilities` grep hits in `packages/react/...` are unrelated imports, not `dateTimeFormat`.)

## 3. Default `style` values and Intl mapping (from source — authoritative)

| Formatter | Fn | Default `style` | Intl mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relative time | `relative.format` | `'short'` | `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` `{ style }`; when `abs(seconds)<45` uses `numeric:'auto'` + `format(0,'seconds')` |
| Absolute time | `absolute.formatTime` | `'medium'` | `{ timeStyle: style, timeZone }` |
| Absolute date | `absolute.formatDate` | `'long'` | `{ dateStyle: style, timeZone }` |
| Date + time | `absolute.format` | timeStyle `'medium'`, dateStyle `'long'` | `style` splits into both; `style:'tooltip'` → `timeStyle:'long', dateStyle:'full'`; explicit `timeStyle`/`dateStyle` override |
| Range | `absolute.formatRange` | timeStyle `'medium'`, dateStyle `'long'` | `timeStyle`/`dateStyle` from `style`; passing `null` for either omits that part; calls `dtf.formatRange` |

Note a discrepancy worth flagging: the module README documents different defaults than the code. README says relative default `"long"` (code `'short'`), time default `"short"` (code `'medium'`), date default `"medium"` (code `'long'`), and combined/range defaults `"short"`/`"medium"` (code `'medium'`/`'long'`). The `.ts` sources above are the real runtime behavior.

## 4. Tests and demos/examples

Tests (co-located, Jest-style `.js`):
- `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/relative-test.js`
- `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/absolute-test.js`

Docs: `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/README.md` (full usage examples for all five, including timezone and range date-only/time-only cases).

Demo/example/story pages: none found. There are no `examples/`, `stories`, `.mdx`, or Storybook files for these utilities anywhere in the repo — usage documentation is confined to the README.

## 5. Where to add a new "duration" formatter

Add it in the same module directory: **`/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/`**.

Following existing conventions:
1. Create `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/duration.ts` exporting a `format(...)` function (likely wrapping `Intl.DurationFormat`), mirroring the `relative.ts` shape with a `{ locale, style }` options object.
2. Register it in the module barrel `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/index.ts`:
   ```ts
   import * as duration from './duration';
   export const dateTimeFormat = { relative, absolute, duration };
   ```
   No change needed to `/app/packages/utilities/src/index.ts` (it re-exports the whole module).
3. Add a co-located test `/app/packages/utilities/src/dateTimeFormat/duration-test.js` and a "Duration" section in the module `README.md`.

Consumers would then use `dateTimeFormat.duration.format(...)` with no package.json/export changes required.
